concepts.def: If God is all-good and all-powerful, why is there suffering?
An attempt to justify God in the face of evil
Evil exists because God gave humans real freedom
Suffering helps humans grow morally (John Hick)
Belief that God's existence cannot be known

walkthroughs.body_html:
Epicurus's classic challenge: if God can stop evil but won't, he's not loving; if he can't, he's not all-powerful.

Natural evil = earthquakes, disease. Moral evil = murder, theft.

This is the strongest objection to theism on the GCSE.

The free will defence (Augustine) says God gave humans real choice; evil is the price of freedom.

The soul-making theodicy (John Hick) says suffering helps us develop courage, compassion and faith.

Christians also point to the cross: God enters human suffering in Jesus.

Richard Dawkins ('The God Delusion', 2006) argues science explains the universe without God, and religion causes harm.

Believers reply: science answers how, religion answers why. The arguments don't prove God beyond doubt — but they make belief reasonable.

mcqs.q: What is the doctrine of the Trinity?
options: Christians believe in three different gods.
God is one being existing in three persons (Father, Son, Holy Spirit) — distinct in person but united in essence; Christians remain monotheistic.
Jesus was a human who became God after his resurrection.
The Trinity refers to heaven, earth and hell.

mcqs.q: What do orthodox Christians believe about the nature of Jesus?
options: The Trinity refers to heaven, earth and hell.
Jesus was half God and half human.
Jesus was a human who became God after his resurrection.
He is fully God and fully human at the same time (the incarnation) — both natures united in one person, as defined at the Council of Chalcedon.

mcqs.q: Is the Buddha a god in Buddhism?
options: Jesus was a human who became God after his resurrection.
The Buddha created the universe.
Buddhists worship the Buddha as their god.

No — the Buddha (Siddhartha Gautama) is regarded as an enlightened human teacher who discovered the path to liberation. Theravada Buddhism is generally non-theistic; some Mahayana traditions develop more elaborate cosmologies.
